topic: Why do video game cities feel alive?
title: Why Video Game Cities Feel So Alive
hook: A great game city feels alive even when you are not looking.

scenes.heading: MORE THAN GRAPHICS
scenes.caption: Realism is not only about sharper textures.
scenes.narration: A great video game city feels alive for reasons that go far beyond graphics.

scenes.heading: NPC ROUTINES
scenes.caption: Characters can follow routines and react to the world.
scenes.narration: Non player characters can follow routines, move through the world, and react to events. Those small behaviours make streets feel populated.

scenes.heading: AMBIENT SOUND
scenes.caption: Traffic, crowds and distant sounds build atmosphere.
scenes.narration: Ambient audio adds another layer. Traffic, conversations, footsteps and distant activity help make a place feel like a functioning city.

scenes.heading: WORLD DETAILS
scenes.caption: Signs, shops and changing environments tell a story.
scenes.narration: Environmental details also matter. Signs, shops, weather and changing locations give each area its own identity.

scenes.heading: THE REAL SECRET
scenes.caption: The world should feel like it exists without you.
scenes.narration: The real trick is making the world feel as though it continues to exist when the player looks away. Which game does this best?

description: An original gaming explainer from Pixel Uncovered. This video discusses general game-design techniques using original narration and graphics.
